body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Service degradation detected: smart-routing anomalies in eu-west and ap-southeast regions. Error spike: 502/timeout and model-mismatch errors reported. Auto-escalating to on-call.

maya: on it — taking incident lead. paging netops and eng-runtime. @josh you up for primary?

josh: I can take primary in 15. starting quick triage now. where's the impact matrix?

product-ops: we have 4 enterprise sessions reporting high latency, at least 2 customers retrying requests and seeing different model outputs mid-session (likely wrong model variant). Tracking AcmePayments as P1.

maya: note: smart-routing logs show repeated fallback between eu-west -> ap-southeast -> eu-west for some sessions. looks like a fallback loop causing duplicate token charges and partial responses.

katie: preliminary theory: DNS endpoints in ap-southeast still resolving to deprecated edge IPs after last config change. smart-routing policy sees unhealthy region and tries fallback variant, but because the edge IPs are stale, the health checks flap and policy re-evaluates -> oscillation.

josh: pulling DNS from affected nodes:
```
dig +short api.redwood-inference.example @8.8.8.8
# returns 3.120.45.8  (stale)
# expected 52.210.12.3 (current)
```

josh: curl headers from client traces show: `X-Route: eu-west-legacy` and `X-Model-Variant: gptx-8bit` while control plane expects `gptx-quant`. mismatch is causing structured output to fail.

netops-bot: running edge purge: `cdnctl purge --zone ap-southeast --hostname api.redwood-inference.example`

netops-bot: purge submitted, returning purge-id=purge-79b2. Waiting for edge invalidation.

emma: adding temporary mitigation: pin smart-routing to prefer static-region eu-west for AcmePayments via runtime override. command: `redwoodctl routing set --session AcmePayments --force-region eu-west --ttl 600`

maya: good. also lowering DNS TTL for affected records to 30s to speed propagation while we fix origin glue. request: ops to push DNS A record update to 52.210.12.3 and ensure authoritative servers updated.

netops-bot: authoritative update propagated to primary nameserver. confirm: `dig +trace api.redwood-inference.example` shows new answer on ns1.verified-hosting.net.

josh: monitoring client retries. error rate falling from 18% -> 4% in eu-west. ap-southeast still shows flapping for ~2% of sessions, likely cached in ISP/edge.

product-ops: notifying AcmePayments SRE and support: we have partial impact, currently mitigated by forced-region routing. they're asking about billing; suggest pausing token billing window for affected timeframe.

maya: on-call handoff in 10 — @josh you'll be primary. I'll stay for coordination and stakeholder comms.

josh: taking primary. checklist: 1) confirm CDN purge completion 2) monitor smart-routing decisions for 10m 3) disable aggressive fallback policy (set max-fallbacks=1) 4) open bridge if oscillation persists.

netops-bot: purge complete across all POPs (ap-southeast included). purge-duration=48s.

katie: updating routing policy to reduce automatic multi-variant fallbacks: `policy update smart-fallback --max-fallbacks 1 --cooldown 120`

josh: applied policy update. sampling logs show fewer fallback attempts. adding quick grep output: `grep "fallback_attempt" routing.log | tail -n 20` shows no repeats for affected sessions.

incident-bot: severity -> SEV3 (customer impact but partial mitigation). pages suppressed for non-oncall channels.

product-ops: AcmePayments confirms degraded but functional flows after forced-region override. asking for ETA for full fix.

maya: ETA: rolling config to authoritative DNS and CDN purged — full global propagation expected within 10-15 minutes. we'll keep forced-region in place for AcmePayments for 1 hour then evaluate.

josh: after 20m of observation error rates stable <1% across regions. removing temporary forced-region for one customer to validate path.

josh: quick post-mit notes: root cause appears to be a stale DNS record on one of our registrar glue servers combined with an overly aggressive fallback policy that didn't respect single-backoff cooldowns, producing a routing oscillation. also model-variant selection logic didn't atomically verify variant compatibility leading to mixed responses.

emma: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime and eng-platform for follow-up. suggested actions in ticket: improve variant compatibility checks, add guardrail to routing policy for TTL-backed actions, and add DNS monitoring alert for stale glue entries.

maya: handing to eng-runtime for postmortem. I'll draft customer comms and coordinate billing adjustments.

josh: closing live mitigation. monitoring window 30m. if no regressions, we'll move to postmortem and action items. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: NOTE: handoff recorded. next on-call: josh. incident thread locked for updates to incident channel only.
